# Exercises

## Exercise 1 — Mixed numeric and character

**Goal:** Observe coercion when a character value is combined with numbers.

```{r ex1-values, eval = FALSE}
1
1L
"C"
typeof(1)
typeof(1L)
typeof("C")
```

> 1 is double, 1L is integer, and "C" is character.

```{r ex1-combined, eval = FALSE}
c(1, 1L, "C")
```

> Since "C" can't possibly be an integer or double, it changes all the data to characters, which can fit them all.

```{r ex1-typeof, eval = FALSE}
typeof(c(1, 1L, "C"))
```

> It is character, because any symbol or combination of symbols can be a character.

## Exercise 2 — Integer sequence and numeric

**Goal:** Observe coercion between integer and double.

```{r ex2-values, eval = FALSE}
1:3
5
typeof(1:3)
typeof(5)
```

> 1:3 = integer
5 = double

```{r ex2-typeof, eval = FALSE}
typeof(c(1:3, 5))
```

> The combined vector is double because it is a more broad type than integer.

## Exercise 3 — Numeric and logical

**Goal:** Observe coercion between numeric and logical values.

```{r ex3-values, eval = FALSE}
3
FALSE
T
typeof(3)
typeof(FALSE)
typeof(T)
```

> 3 = double
FALSE & T= logical

```{r ex3-typeof, eval = FALSE}
typeof(c(3, FALSE, T))
```

> It is double because logical vectors can be represented with 1s and 0s.

## Exercise 4 — Logical and explicit numeric coercion

**Goal:** Observe the effect of `as.numeric()` on a logical value.

```{r ex4-values, eval = FALSE}
TRUE
as.numeric(TRUE)
typeof(TRUE)
typeof(1)
```

> TRUE = Logical
1 = double

```{r ex4-typeof, eval = FALSE}
typeof(c(TRUE, as.numeric(TRUE)))
```

> It is double because 1 represents true and 0 represesnts false.

## Exercise 5 — Missing, logical, and coerced logical

**Goal:** Observe coercion involving `NA` and logical values.

```{r ex5-values, eval = FALSE}
NA
FALSE
as.logical(1)
typeof(NA)
```

> They are all logical after using "as.logical"

```{r ex5-typeof, eval = FALSE}
typeof(c(NA, FALSE, as.logical(1)))
```

> It's all logical because NA and FALSE themselves are logical, while the 1 becomes logical because of the "as.logical" function.

## Exercise 6 — Division by zero and character

**Goal:** Observe coercion when an infinite numeric value is combined with a character.

```{r ex6-values, eval = FALSE}
1L
0
1L / 0
"A"
typeof(1L)
typeof(0)
typeof(Inf)
typeof("A")
```

> 1L = integer
0 = double
Inf = double
"A" = character

```{r ex6-typeof, eval = FALSE}
typeof(c(1L / 0, "A"))
```

> The combined vector is a character, this is because the character type is the most general type or lowest common denominator if you will.

## Exercise 7 — Glimpse the earthquakes data

**Goal:** Inspect the structure of a real data frame.

```{r glimpse-earthquakes, eval = FALSE}
glimpse(earthquakes)
```

## Exercise 8 — Variables that can be coerced without loss

**Goal:** Identify columns whose type can change without losing information.

> You could change both year and day to integer without losing information.

## Exercise 9 — Visualization problems from type coercion

**Goal:** Anticipate plotting issues caused by an incorrect type.

> This would create an issue because the years would be unorganized since its a character type instead of a double type, so it might not list them in order on the graph the same way.

## Exercise 10 — Create and filter a major-earthquake indicator

**Goal:** Build a logical indicator, coerce it to numeric, and filter.

```{r major-earthquakes, eval = FALSE}
earthquakes %>% 
  mutate(major = case_when(
    richter > 7.5 ~ TRUE,
    TRUE ~ FALSE
  )) %>% 
  mutate(major = as.numeric(major)) %>% 
  filter(major == 1)
```

**Question:** How many major earthquakes are there in this dataset?

> 29
